found_without_a_rule: CORRECTION of my round-1 report: I wrote that the 'Par Amount / Shares' figure on the PIK preferred rows is a dollar amount. The schedule note in every filing says equity is recorded as number of shares owned, so the figures are counts by the filer's statement and are now published as counts. Growth at the PIK rate (Class B 6,314 / 6,950 / 7,535 / 8,162) fits PIK paid in further shares as well as it fits an accreting amount; the page does not settle it beyond the note.

Protective Industrial Products Series A Preferred: the filer prints the count in two scales (30, 31, 31, then 31,597 at 2023-12-31, then 33, 34, 36, 37, 38; cost 29.5M to 38.2M, so the small figures are thousands of shares). Published as printed and tagged in each quarter except 2023-12-31, where the unit-scale normaliser publishes 31 for the tagged and printed 31,597 (labelled derived_proxy). The series is 1,000 times too small against the footnote's 'number of shares' in every quarter but that one; not changed, because the page prints those figures.

The unit-scale normaliser (pipeline/unified_holdings.py, shares_held:pow10_shares) compares price per unit across all rows of one issuer, so a warrant beside a preferred of the same issuer was given the preferred's count (Metropolis 2024-09-30, corrected in round 1). Shared code, not changed; other funds not measured. It runs before row corrections, so the 23 counts set in round 2 are not touched by it (checked: all 23 publish the corrected value).

Metropolis warrant: 4 units against a cost of 189 thousand and a fair value of up to 1,896 thousand; Class D preferred: 24 against 778. Published as printed; whether the filer means 4 and 24 or thousands is not on the page.
The two declared Mattress Firm pars carry principal_amount_source 'xbrl_field' although the value comes from the page (label written by the shared declared-value path).
Ligado Networks first lien loan: the 10-Qs for 2024-06-30 and 2024-09-30 print '15.50 %' without 'PIK'; published pik_rate is empty in those two quarters and 15.5 in the others. As printed.
